$comment: UI <-> host message contract, v2. Single source of truth, owned by the host (C#) side. Deliberately WIDE: it names every command the HMI will ever emit in this phase; hosts that do not implement a command MUST still ack it with response{success:false, code:'notSupported'}. The gate (tools/check_contract.mjs) fails CI if the frontend emits a command not declared here. The internal viewer<->slicer postMessage bridge (source:'meltio-slicer') is NOT part of this contract: it never crosses the UI<->host boundary.

shape.requestId: string, only on command and its response

ackCodes.$comment: response.code values a UI must handle for any command.

permissionLevels.$comment: Minimum sign-in level a host must enforce server-side for motion-bearing commands. UI gating is a convenience, never the boundary.

shell.$comment: HMI UI <-> host. Today: FastAPI dev-host (POST /api/machine/command et al). Tomorrow: WebView2 CoreWebView2MainChannel.

uiReady.note: completes host WaitForReadyAsync; host answers with init

resetCameraHome.note: camera/scene preset, not machine motion. Renamed from 'homePosition' in this revision: it sat between 'home'/'homeXY'/'homeZ', which DO move axes, and nothing has ever emitted it. The viewer channel keeps its own 'homePosition' message - that channel has no machine commands to be confused with

pausePrint.note: de-escalating: always allowed for a signed-in operator

ackData.user: {id, username, name, roleId, roleName, rank, permissions[]}

jog.note: the upper bound is the largest step the jog pad offers (urdf.html data-move-step). A host MUST reject anything outside it: this is the one command whose magnitude comes straight from a touch target

driveFeeder.note: drives the feeder wheel. This IS what the HMI emits and what a handler answers; 'FEEDER' used to be listed as an alias of loadFeeder, which shares none of its params - two different operations paired on the word 'feeder'

loadFeeder.note: load material into a feeder. Nothing emits it and no handler exists; kept as the wide-contract placeholder the $comment authorises. It lost its 'FEEDER' alias - see driveFeeder

emergencyStop.note: always allowed, from any state, signed-in or not

payload.signals: { emergencyStopActive, machineArmedRequired, machineArmedState, inertedSystemActive, filtrationRequired, controllerBoardConnected, gasFlowLow, gasFlowDecreasing, coolantFlowLow, closedLoopFault, externalSecurityFault, softwareUpdateAvailable, firmwareUpdateAvailable, internetConnected, preventiveMaintenanceDue, doorsClosed, laserHeadReady: boolean|null; coolantTemperature: number|null }

machineState.note: telemetry snapshot; replaces the HMI's 60fps DOM readout loops - UI updates on this event
machineState.$revision: 'signals' and 'activeCodes' used to read 'object' and 'string[]'. Both were wrong, and a host cannot discover either from the wire because both fail SILENTLY. activeCodes: the HMI reads item.class/item.code (hmi/ports/machineLink.js), so a bare string array raises no fault at all - and MeltioErrors.raise has exactly one caller, that reconcile loop, so a contract-faithful host loses every fault the machine reports. signals: the pre-print interlock takes live telemetry VERBATIM and fails closed on missing keys, so a partial object blocks printing with no explanation. The keys above are the full set the HMI knows (hmi/notifications.js mockNotificationSignals); send them all.

payload.user: {id, username, name, roleId, roleName, rank, permissions[]}|null

viewer.$comment: Host <-> Three.js viewer iframe. No requestId on this channel.

setSafeArea.note: occluded screen edges (top bar, bottom nav, docked panels). Replaces the viewer reading host DOM rects for camera framing/scene shift - the host owns layout

machineState.note: drives in-scene motion (gantry, doors, feeders) instead of viewer-local mock state
